text: Michael’s strokes over nine holes: 3, 4, 3, 5, 3, 2, 4, 5, 4. Use median-of-halves quartiles, excluding the overall median when the number of data values is odd. Find the lower and upper quartiles.
html:
Michael’s strokes over nine holes: 3, 4, 3, 5, 3, 2, 4, 5, 4. Use median-of-halves quartiles, excluding the overall median when the number of data values is odd.

Find the lower and upper quartiles.
answerHtml:
Worked solution

Exclude the overall median. Lower half: 2,3,3,3, so Q1=3. Upper half: 4,4,5,5, so Q3=(4+5)/2 = 4.5.

text: Adam and Josie record spending for ten days, rounded to the nearest $5. Compare the two spending patterns using measures of centre and spread.
html:
Adam and Josie record spending for ten days, rounded to the nearest $5.

PersonDaily spending ($)
Adam15, 30, 10, 20, 210, 20, 15, 15, 30, 25
Josie45, 55, 60, 20, 30, 30, 35, 25, 20, 70

Compare the two spending patterns using measures of centre and spread.
answerHtml:
Worked solution

Josie has a higher median ($32.50 versus $20) and larger IQR ($30 versus $15), so her typical spending is higher and her middle half is more variable. Adam has a much higher maximum ($210) and range ($200 versus $50), driven by an unusually large day. Their means are similar: Adam $39 and Josie $39, illustrating the effect of Adam’s extreme value.
